Use case: style-transfer. Edit this existing VIGINTI game concept. Preserve the seated tilted-table camera, the three playable hand bays with clear rank indices, dealer pair at rear, six side relic positions, DRAW and STAND actions. Primary change: completely replace its expensive realistic antique brass casino look with a boldly GRAPHIC, LIMITED-INK RISOGRAPH 3D CUT-PAPER MUNICIPAL OFFICE. All objects have flat matte color faces and simple graphic geometry, printed ink grain and occasional offset registration in decorative graphics. Four dominant inks: pale mint, butter paper, coral vermilion, midnight navy. Shadows are one flat navy ink value. Like a physical paper maquette of an absurd public-service office, dimensional folded paper, corrugated card edges, linocut print, broad untextured fields with restrained speckle. NO photoreal metal, NO realistic wood, NO gold, NO ornate serif casino borders, NO luxurious plaque, NO polished surfaces. Camera perspective and cast shadows show this is still a playable 3D space.
Office uses blunt bureaucratic grid, tabular numbers, narrow grotesk typography, utilitarian paper form lines. VIGINTI is modest block sans lettering on a printed desk name tent. Left backdrop is flat printed institutional graphic; a label reads "MINISTRY OF TWENTY", rear label "FORM XX". Frosted window simplified to grey-blue paper rectangle with a barely-seen clerical silhouette. Fan is folded-paper sculptural prop. Six side relics become chunky rubber stamps with red wood handles and black bases, each distinct silhouette, rather than bronze casino charms. Front buttons become flat coral and navy plastic tabs printed DRAW and STAND. Three player bays are cream government forms. A red APPROVED stamp beside the winning central A/K hand. Rank and suit indices stay DARK NAVY and RED with sharp print. Do not put ANTE or separate wagers under every hand; this game has one round ante. Leave room between dealer and player bays for one cream draw card (4 hearts) centered, slightly lifted casting a graphic shadow. Minimal, ludicrously official, tactile PAPER, striking editorial art direction. Keep 16:9 single gameplay scene, no captions or surrounding presentation board.

Use case: style-transfer. Edit this VIGINTI clay mythology gameplay concept. Keep its same clear three player hand bays, dealer pair, centre draw card, six relic niches, 3D perspective table composition and readable ordinary playing cards, VIGINTI lettering, DRAW and STAND buttons. Primary change: make this unmistakably a tiny CHEAP HANDMADE STOP-MOTION SET in a SHOEBOX, not an actual wealthy Roman temple. The mythical grandeur should be funny because it is visibly constructed from plasticine, painted corrugated cardboard, blue paper, tape and scraps.
Replace realistic distant mountains and temples with a single crooked ultramarine painted cardboard sky backdrop showing its cut top edge and a raw corrugated side wall, behind which a plain warm studio wall peeks. Two clouds are obviously paper cutouts dangling on visible cotton threads. The columns are stubby lumpy finger-sculpted cream plasticine mounted on bottlecaps, tilted slightly. Retain tiny blue canopy but make it an uneven fabric scrap clipped with a clothespin at one corner. Central clay dealer should be smaller and more lumpy, pear-shaped bust, big resigned nose, sleepy eyelids, misaligned wonky laurel crown. His throne has cardboard edges and little pieces of visible repair tape. Six side relics are little lumpy colored clay votives in chipped clay niches, not elaborate realistic statues. The tabletop is warm terracotta colored plasticine slab, rounded smeared edges, obvious thumbprints and tool marks, with paper playing cards on top. Reduce the ornamental grandeur, shorten the pediment, sculpt the VIGINTI letters a little crooked.
Lighting remains soft miniature studio lighting, colors terracotta/apricot/ultramarine/chalk/teal. Strong tactile shallow fingerprint bump and clay compression. Matte, substantial physical forms, no smooth plastic mobile-game gloss, no realistic marble. All gameplay sharp and all card rank corners readable. This should be an artist-built miniature you could pick up in two hands, intimate, silly and lovingly overdramatic. Landscape 16:9 single scene.

Use case: style-transfer. Edit this VIGINTI game-show screenshot concept. Keep its excellent exact composition and all gameplay arrangements: tilted orange turquoise contestant console, three white card hand bays, dealer pair at rear, center draw position, deck at right, six absurd prize relics along side rims, DRAW/STAND buttons, giant VIGINTI marquee, cardboard sunburst host, APPLAUSE sign and backstage equipment. Primary change: apply decisively NONPHOTOREALISTIC THREE-TONE CEL SHADING across the entire game world. Flat persimmon orange, turquoise, mustard, cream and plum bands; hard posterized shadow boundaries; thin deep plum outlines around 3D object silhouettes; white graphic highlight shapes on trim instead of realistic reflective metal. Replace fine vinyl/metal surface noise with limited bold screenprint halftone dots confined to selected shadow bands. Do not merely add outlines to realistic surfaces. It should look like an actual gorgeous playable cel-shaded 3D cartoon, not a studio photo, not realistic 3D game-engine PBR.
Keep spatial geometry and physical contact shadows; keep world tilted and dimensional. Card faces themselves remain unshaded cream with very crisp dark/red rank and suit print for legibility. The flat cardboard smiling host should visibly have a thin cut edge and one taped rear support peeking at its side, not become a full sculptural character. Selective bright warm bloom only around marquee bulbs and the APPLAUSE lamp, no glare on cards. Clear larger solid color shapes, cheerful underfunded TV studio. Do not add more text or cover cards with particles. No captions, no title board, one landscape 16:9 game view.
